skim: Brazil’s cliffhanger election went to the polls with Lula clinging to a narrow lead over Bolsonaro’s son, DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak showed its first signs of easing even as the toll held above 4,000, and a flash flood buried a Spanish town as a new storm system lingered.

Ethiopia’s Tigray militia claimed near-total control as the civil war reignited, Iran readied for a “major round of fighting” as Trump weighed new strikes after the midterms, and Sudan’s army seized the RSF’s largest North Kordofan stronghold.

The White House ordered federal agencies to rebrand “AI” as “Super Intelligence,” Paramount Skydance prepared to close its $110 billion Warner Bros. Discovery merger Monday, and Nvidia unveiled a $4,999 desktop AI system as global M&A activity fell 41% to $993 billion in Q3.

India edged Pakistan by 19 runs to win Asian Games cricket gold, Saudi Arabia and the UAE booked their places in Tuesday’s Gulf Cup final, and Max Verstappen snatched his first pole of the season at Sepang.

UK diesel breached £2 a litre for the first time, a second tanker was struck east of Oman hours after the original Hormuz attack, and India’s SIR electoral-roll protests spread to Mumbai and Kolkata as violence erupted in Birati.

stories.headline: Brazil heads to polls in cliffhanger election pitting Lula against Bolsonaro’s son
stories.body: Brazilians vote today in the first round between 80-year-old Lula and 45-year-old Flávio Bolsonaro, with polls split — Quaest has Lula ahead 37%-33%, while AtlasIntel puts it within three points at 46%-43% — per Al Jazeera (Oct 3). Voting runs 8am–5pm Brasília time, with a runoff set for Oct 25 if neither clears a majority; Flávio told supporters he is praying “for the opportunity to walk up the ramp of Planalto Palace next year alongside” his imprisoned father. The vote follows Thursday’s cancelled televised debate and a bomb scare outside Brazil’s Supreme Court.

stories.headline: DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak shows signs of easing even as toll holds above 4,000
stories.body: The death toll in DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak stands at 4,018 with 8,300 confirmed cases, but health authorities say 12 of the 63 affected health zones have now gone weeks without a new case, with transmission “confined to specific zones” after intensified containment, per CGTN (Oct 3). More than 2,162 patients have recovered from the Bundibugyo strain, for which no vaccine or treatment is yet approved.

stories.headline: Deadly flash flood buries Spanish town as new storm system lingers
stories.body: A 102-year-old woman died and roughly 90 people were rescued after a DANA storm dumped 140mm of rain on Madrigueras, in Spain’s Albacete province, in just over two hours Friday night, per The Watchers (Oct 3). Mayor Juan Carlos Talavera said four homes collapsed and more than 150 flooded vehicles were towed away, with forecasters warning the unstable Mediterranean moisture plume would persist through Oct 4.

stories.headline: Gulf of Mexico watched for first tropical system as hurricane-free streak nears its end
stories.body: The US National Hurricane Center is tracking a 20% chance of tropical development in the southwestern Gulf of Mexico over the next week, even as wind shear from the subtropical jet stream threatens to tear apart any system before it can organize, per WITN (Oct 4). The region remains on course for a rare hurricane-free Atlantic season — only the third on record, after 1907 and 1914 — though forecasters note any system would still raise moisture and rainfall across the southeastern US.

stories.headline: India edge Pakistan by 19 runs to win Asian Games cricket gold
stories.body: Batting first at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin, India posted 211 and held Pakistan to 192, with Abhishek Sharma’s blistering 61 off 28 balls (three fours, seven sixes) setting the tone before Jasprit Bumrah and Axar Patel shared the key wickets in a 19-run win, per Al Jazeera (Oct 3). Pakistan’s chase briefly rallied through Saim Ayub (29 off 22) and Hasan Nawaz (28 off 20) in a 50-run stand, but sharp Indian fielding closed it out to settle the first-ever Asian Games cricket gold medal decider between the rivals, per Outlook India (Oct 3).

stories.headline: Shai Hope’s unbeaten 162 sinks India in West Indies dead-rubber classic
stories.body: West Indies chased down 352 with five wickets and ten balls to spare at New Chandigarh’s PCA Stadium, as Shai Hope finished unbeaten on 162 off 143 balls (17 fours, three sixes) with Amir Jangoo adding 67, per Outlook India (Oct 3). India had posted 351/7 behind KL Rahul’s unbeaten 129 off 87 balls and Rohit Sharma’s 92, but the dead-rubber loss didn’t cost India the series, which it had already sealed 2-0 after Gill’s record double-century in Guwahati; the final tally finished 2-1.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia edge Qatar on penalties, UAE see off Oman to set up Gulf Cup final
stories.body: Saudi Arabia beat hosts Qatar 3-2 on penalties after a goalless 120 minutes at King Abdullah Sports City in Jeddah, while the UAE had earlier edged Oman 1-0 through an Ousmane Camara header, despite Nicolas Gimenez missing a 56th-minute penalty, per The Peninsula Qatar (Oct 4) and Asharq Al-Awsat (Oct 3). UAE coach Zlatko Dalic said, “we never gave up… we worked hard for the last 20 days for this night, for this game,” as Saudi Arabia and the UAE now meet in Tuesday’s final back in Jeddah.

stories.headline: Verstappen snatches maiden pole of the season at Sepang
stories.body: Max Verstappen topped qualifying for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia in 1:35.130, edging Lewis Hamilton’s Ferrari by 0.298s, with Kimi Antonelli and Charles Leclerc completing the top four, per Formula1.com (Oct 3). “It’s fantastic… we’ve been trying many Grands Prix to get pole, sometimes a bit closer than others, but to finally get it from where we started the season, it’s pretty incredible,” Verstappen said, as Isack Hadjar dropped to P8 after a five-place grid penalty ahead of Sunday’s race at Sepang.

stories.headline: Paramount Skydance to close $110B Warner Bros. Discovery merger Monday, rebrand as ‘Skydance’
stories.body: Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery confirmed their merger will close October 6, creating a combined media giant valued at roughly $110 billion in enterprise value ($81 billion in equity) that will operate under a new corporate name, Skydance, per TechCrunch (Oct 2). The deal brings together Paramount+, HBO Max, CBS, CNN, MTV and franchises including “The Lord of the Rings” and “Game of Thrones” after a federal judge this week approved a settlement with the 12-state coalition of attorneys general that had challenged the deal on competition grounds. “We never wanted a new corporate identity to diminish, alter or overshadow either one,” said David Ellison, who will lead the combined company, of keeping the Paramount and Warner Bros. brands prominent.

stories.headline: Global M&A falls 41% to $993B in Q3 as borrowing costs bite
stories.body: Global takeover activity dropped 41% quarter-on-quarter to $993 billion in the third quarter — the first sub-$1 trillion quarter in over a year — even as full-year 2026 deal value held at $3.9 trillion, the highest since 2001, per Reuters data carried by Global Banking & Finance Review (Oct 1). The 10-year US Treasury yield’s climb to 5.34%, its highest since 2002, is the main drag; Morgan Stanley’s John Collins said higher yields make “valuations sometimes a little tougher,” while Clifford Chance’s Sarah Jones called the pullback “a normalization rather than an end of a cycle.” Technology remains the busiest sector, accounting for roughly a quarter of global deal value as AI and data-center tie-ups dominate, alongside megadeals like Banca Monte dei Paschi’s $32 billion bid for Banco BPM.

stories.headline: Airtel Money opens retail offer, applications close Oct 8 ahead of London listing
stories.body: Airtel Money’s London IPO formally opened to retail investors following its October 1 prospectus, with a £250 minimum application against the already-set £1.96 share price — still implying the £5.3 billion ($7 billion) valuation — and the offer closing October 8 at 5pm with results due October 9, per BusinessPost Nigeria (Oct 2). An extra 27 million existing shares can be released if demand is oversubscribed beyond the 270 million shares on offer, with trading still set to begin October 14 on the London Stock Exchange’s Main Market at a 16.5% public float; Airtel Africa said it intends to “remain a long-term strategic shareholder” as Airtel Money becomes an independently listed business.

stories.headline: Sensex, Nifty log 8th straight weekly loss as FIIs sell & Brent tops $100
stories.body: India’s Sensex closed the week at 71,909.70 (down 2.7%) and the Nifty 50 at 22,421.95 (down 3.1%), extending the benchmarks’ losing streak to eight consecutive weeks — the longest in 25 years — as foreign institutional investors sold a net ₹34,966 crore of equities in a seventh straight week of outflows, per Goodreturns (Oct 3). Brent crude’s climb above $100 a barrel on West Asia tensions is squeezing India as a net oil importer, with Master Capital Services’ Chief Research Officer Dr. Ravi Singh warning that “a decisive break below [22,250] could intensify selling pressure and open the way towards 22,000.”

stories.headline: Musk confirms TSMC talks for Terafab, his dedicated Tesla-SpaceX-xAI chip plant
stories.body: Elon Musk confirmed talks are underway for TSMC to help build and operate Terafab, the Texas chip facility he’s setting up to exclusively supply Tesla, SpaceX and xAI, saying only “just discussions, but something may come of it,” per Tom’s Hardware (Oct 3). Under one option reportedly being explored, TSMC would own and operate the plant while SpaceX commits to chip purchases; under another, SpaceX would hold majority ownership with TSMC providing process technology, potentially displacing Intel, which currently supplies its 1.4nm-class 14A process to the $16.8 billion project.

stories.headline: OpenAI’s new always-on ‘Dots’ agent stumbles in live DevDay demo
stories.body: OpenAI unveiled Dots, persistent AI agents built on its GPT-6 Astra model that keep working after a chat window closes, connect to up to 4,000 apps and operate inside their own cloud computer and browser — part of 20-plus announcements at DevDay 2026 that also included GPT-6.1 Sol and a new collaborative “ChatGPT Space.” During the live demo an agent nicknamed “Dottie” froze for roughly ten seconds when asked for a testing update, an on-stage stumble that underscored reliability concerns even as CEO Sam Altman described Dots as something that will “soon be available on other messaging apps and even over the phone as an audio model,” per American Bazaar (Oct 1). The first Dot is free for Pro and Business Premium subscribers, with Enterprise, Edu and Healthcare tiers getting phased beta access.

stories.headline: White House orders federal agencies to rebrand ‘AI’ as ‘Super Intelligence’
stories.body: Executive Order 14434, “Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence,” signed September 29 and reported Oct 2, directs the federal executive branch to replace “Artificial Intelligence” and “AI” with “Super Intelligence” and “SI” in official correspondence, reports and policy documents going forward, per Forbes (Oct 2). The order gives agencies 60 days to draft a new federal definition of SI — defaulting to the existing statutory AI definition in the meantime — which legal analysts warn could spark court disputes if the new term later diverges from existing contracts, vendor agreements and state or municipal rules that still reference “AI.”

stories.headline: AWS pledges $1B for data-center communities as it warns US ‘can’t afford to lose’ AI race
stories.body: Amazon Web Services pledged $1 billion over five years for communities hosting its data centers — covering education, job training, energy affordability and water preservation — as pushback mounts: 30 states have introduced data-center legislation and local opposition has blocked 45 proposed developments across 27 states, per CBS News (Oct 2). AWS CEO Matt Garman framed the buildout as a geopolitical imperative, warning “a lapse in our nation’s focus or resolve could put us behind” in AI leadership, and suggested foreign actors may be “seeding misinformation” to slow US data-center growth.

stories.headline: Tigray militia claims near-total control as Ethiopia’s civil war reignites
stories.body: The government-aligned Tigray Peace Forces say they have driven out the Tigray People’s Liberation Front and taken near-total control of the Tigray region, with its commander declaring TPLF forces “wiped out” in a Thursday social media post, per Al Jazeera (Oct 2). Residents report federal forces closing in on regional capital Mekelle as fighting — which resumed after a 2022 peace deal collapsed and a seven-group opposition alliance formed on Sept 20 — leaves Tigray’s 6-7 million residents under electricity and internet blackouts, according to Al Jazeera Arabic’s Ethiopia bureau chief Mohammed Taha Tawakel.

stories.headline: Iran readies for ‘major round of fighting’ as Trump weighs new strikes after midterms
stories.body: A Tehran source told The National (Oct 3) that Iran “is preparing for a 'major round of fighting'” even as it keeps a diplomatic channel open, having proposed moving its 60%-enriched uranium stockpile to a third party and a seven-day plan to ease Strait of Hormuz tensions — a US counterproposal Iran is unlikely to accept. Trump told reporters it is “possible” he ramps up bombing after the Nov 3 midterms and warned over the FlyDubai cockpit attack, “they’ll be hit very hard, don’t worry,” per The New Arab (Oct 1-2), as the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier group steams toward a Gulf buildup already topping 50,000 US personnel.

stories.headline: Russia kills 8 in fresh barrage as Ukraine’s bridges, grid take new hits
stories.body: Russia fired 157 Shahed and decoy drones overnight, of which Ukraine intercepted 131, killing at least 8 people and injuring 83 across 12 struck locations, per Kyiv Independent (Oct 3). Kharkiv took the worst of it — 5 killed, 49 injured, including from glide bombs — while Kyiv’s Northern Bridge over the Dnipro was struck and Sumy Oblast lost 3 more lives, extending the energy-grid campaign that has already forced emergency power cuts nationwide.

stories.headline: Gaza strike kills five in Gaza City as post-ceasefire toll tops 1,400
stories.body: An Israeli strike hit an apartment building in Gaza City, killing at least five Palestinians, the territory’s health ministry said, per Al Arabiya (Oct 3). The dead bring the toll since the October 2025 ceasefire to more than 1,400 Palestinians and four Israeli soldiers, as the truce remains unresolved over Hamas disarmament and an Israeli withdrawal — Israel accuses Hamas of rearming, which Hamas denies while accusing Israel of undermining the deal.

stories.headline: Sudan’s army seizes RSF’s largest North Kordofan stronghold
stories.body: Sudan’s armed forces captured al-Mazroub, which a military source called “the RSF’s largest stronghold in North Kordofan,” per Al Jazeera (Oct 2). Special Forces spokesman Mohammed Deidan said the town “links the states of North Kordofan and West Kordofan,” advancing the army’s campaign to cut RSF supply lines between army-held central Sudan and the RSF’s Darfur strongholds, in fighting the military says inflicted “heavy combat vehicle losses” on the paramilitary force.

fixtures.headline: Bahrain Grand Prix Race Day (Sepang)
fixtures.body: Race day at Sepang, Malaysia, after Verstappen claimed pole — the first Bahrain-branded F1 race held outside Bahrain.

fixtures.headline: Gulf Cup 27 Final: Saudi Arabia v UAE
fixtures.body: The two semi-final winners meet at King Abdullah Sports City in Jeddah for the title.

fixtures.headline: Australia’s Tour of South Africa, 1st Test
fixtures.body: Five-day series opener at Kingsmead in Durban, the first of a multi-Test tour.

fixtures.headline: Singapore Grand Prix
fixtures.body: Next stop on the calendar after the Sepang weekend, under the Marina Bay lights.

fixtures.headline: Champions League Matchday 2
fixtures.body: League-phase action resumes after the opening round played in mid-September.

portfolio.headline: Nvidia unveils $4,999 DGX Spark desktop AI system to widen access to local AI development
portfolio.body: Nvidia introduced a 64GB configuration of its DGX Spark desktop AI system, priced from $4,999 and set to begin shipping October 23 through OEM partners including Dell, HP, Acer, ASUS, Gigabyte and MSI, per TechAeris (Oct 3). The unit pairs a 20-core Arm CPU with unified memory — expandable to 128GB via clustering — and ships preloaded with Nvidia’s CUDA-X stack, Nemotron and agent-development tools aimed at running large language models and multi-step AI agents entirely on a local desktop.

portfolio.headline: Boeing averts SPEEA strike as engineers ratify four-year contract with 10% raise
portfolio.body: Boeing’s SPEEA-represented engineers and technicians voted to ratify new four-year contracts carrying an immediate 10% raise effective October 2 and a further 4% increase next March, averting a strike that had been set for October 6, per Leeham News (Oct 1). Boeing chief engineer Ben Nimmergut said the company looks forward “to working with our team to support our company’s continued recovery,” and Jefferies analyst Sheila Kahyaoglu reaffirmed a Buy rating with a $265 price target, citing the deal’s stabilizing effect on 737 and 777X production lines, per GuruFocus (Oct 1).

portfolio.headline: J&J’s ICOTYDE shows durable psoriasis clearance through two years in Phase 3 data
portfolio.body: Johnson & Johnson’s oral peptide ICOTYDE (icotrokinra) sustained skin clearance at two years in the Phase 3 ICONIC-TOTAL study, with 70% of patients reaching clear or almost-clear skin (IGA 0/1) and high-impact sites faring even better — 89% complete clearance in genital psoriasis and 60% in scalp psoriasis — per the company’s announcement (Oct 2). Dr. Richard Warren of the University of Manchester called the results “a pivotal advancement in plaque psoriasis treatment,” while J&J global immunology head Dr. David Lee said the data “empower physicians to treat high-impact sites” with confidence in sustained outcomes.

portfolio.headline: Bernstein reiterates Uber Outperform as robotaxi footprint set to hit 15 cities by year-end
portfolio.body: Bernstein SocGen Group reiterated an Outperform rating on Uber with a $95 price target, citing the company’s plan to operate autonomous-vehicle rides in 15 cities — six in the US and nine abroad — by the end of 2026, per Investing.com (Sept 30). The note framed Uber as an aggregator of self-driving technology rather than a developer of it, pointing to partnerships with Nuro in the Bay Area and Houston, Zoox in Las Vegas and Los Angeles, and Wayve in London and Tokyo.

portfolio.headline: Cloudflare data: AI bots now drive 57% of web traffic, arriving years ahead of forecast
portfolio.body: Cloudflare disclosed that AI agents and other bots now generate roughly 57% of web requests across its network — a threshold CEO Matthew Prince said arrived in May, more than a year ahead of his own prior forecast of late 2027, per Yahoo Finance (Oct 1). The shift is also lifting rival infrastructure providers: Akamai disclosed an $11.6 billion, seven-year compute commitment from Anthropic on September 24, underscoring how bot and agent traffic is reshaping demand across the content-delivery sector that includes Fastly.

portfolio.headline: Coeur Mining targets 630,000 oz of gold for 2026 as newly acquired Canadian mines ramp up
portfolio.body: Coeur Mining is ramping up its New Gold-acquired Rainy River mine in Ontario toward 5,000 tonnes per day by year-end, while the New Afton mine in British Columbia lifts output as its C-Zone block-cave operation matures, per Yahoo Finance (Sept 30). The company reiterated 2026 guidance of roughly 630,000 ounces of gold, 19 million ounces of silver and 40 million pounds of copper, with CEO Mitchell Krebs noting that 2027 should see a full year of production from the newly acquired assets.

stories.headline: SIR protests spread to Mumbai and Kolkata as violence erupts in Birati
stories.body: Protests against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls widened beyond Friday’s Jantar Mantar detentions, with thousands rallying at Mumbai’s Shivaji Park — including actors Naseeruddin Shah and Shabana Azmi — while a CPM-SFI “Save Democracy” meeting in Birati, West Bengal, turned violent, per WION (Oct 3). CPM’s Dipsita Dhar said “some BJP-backed miscreants arrived at the meeting and started vandalising the venue,” a charge BJP leader Debashis Chowdhury denied, saying protesters were “hurling foul abuse at the BJP and shouting anti-national slogans” — while Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis said the opposition’s “fake narrative has been exposed by the Election Commission.”

stories.headline: Modi hails India’s Asian Games cricket gold over Pakistan as ‘joyous occasion’
stories.body: PM Narendra Modi congratulated India’s men’s cricket team after it beat Pakistan by 19 runs to retain Asian Games gold in Nisshin, Japan — Abhishek Sharma hit 61 and Tilak Varma an unbeaten 51 in India’s 211/6 — writing, “The Gold comes to India yet again! Congratulations to our Men’s Cricket Team on retaining their title at the Asian Games. This is indeed a joyous occasion for the nation,” per Free Press Journal (Oct 3). Modi added his “best wishes to the team members for their future endeavours,” part of a wider round of congratulations as India also claimed gold in boxing, hockey and wrestling on the Games’ final day.

stories.headline: Al Jazeera profile names FlyDubai attacker as Omani barred over ‘extremist views’
stories.body: A new Al Jazeera profile identifies the co-pilot who attacked Captain Smit Machchhar with a crash axe as Hamam al-Hammami, an Omani citizen born in the UAE to a Syrian mother who spent seven years at Oman Air before Muscat barred him from flying over concerns about extremist views, per Al Jazeera (Oct 3). Al-Hammami had also flown briefly for Royal Air Maroc and completed a distance-learning aviation management course in the UK; Machchhar, who survived the September 30 attack on Flight FZ1073 as the aircraft plunged 17,000 feet, recalled, “I knew that the aircraft was going down… I told myself that the door is right there, just open it.”

stories.headline: India exports Akash air-defence missiles to Armenia, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan
stories.body: India has begun exporting its indigenous Akash medium-range surface-to-air missile system — with a 25-kilometre engagement radius — to Armenia, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan, with Armenia as the first customer, per WION’s Gravitas (Oct 3). India’s defence exports hit over $4 billion in FY2025-26, up 62% year-on-year, with BrahMos cruise missile sales alone projected to top $600 million; New Delhi is targeting ₹50,000 crore in defence exports by 2030 and reports additional interest from Brazil, Egypt and the Philippines.

stories.headline: Dual UK-Iranian national, 27, arrested in London over RAF Fairford plot
stories.body: Counter-terror police arrested a 27-year-old dual UK-Iranian national in London on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts linked to the RAF Fairford incident, with a second British man, 26, questioned separately, per ABC News (Oct 2). It follows the Sunday arrest and bail of five men near the base — where only petrol, not explosives, was found in their vehicles — as Senior National Coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing Vicki Evans said “the investigation into circumstances surrounding events in Gloucestershire is hugely complex, and our specialist teams are interrogating multiple lines of enquiry.” PM Andy Burnham reiterated that authorities “believe Iran to have played a part.”

stories.headline: UK diesel breaches £2 a litre for the first time
stories.body: Average UK diesel prices hit a record 200.01p a litre, edging past Thursday’s 199.79p high, as Britain joins Ireland, France and Italy in emergency talks with Brussels over releasing stockpiles, per ITV News (Oct 2). RAC head of policy Simon Williams said, “This is a pump price threshold that no-one wanted to cross… heaping more misery onto motorists,” with diesel now 57.6p more expensive than when the US-Iran war began in February, adding £32 to the cost of filling an average family car.

stories.headline: Burnham weighs rejoining the EU as government maps out options
stories.body: PM Andy Burnham is drawing up three options for Britain’s relationship with the EU — full membership, a Single Market/customs union arrangement, or the status quo — to present ahead of a November EU-UK summit in Brussels, per Euronews (Oct 2). “We have to look at what is doable and what would be the pros and cons of each,” Burnham said, as MEP Sandro Gozi responded that “Burnham now needs to clarify what he means,” while Centre for European Reform director Charles Grant called the shift “a moral boost for leaders” on the continent.

stories.headline: Second tanker struck east of Oman hours after Hormuz attack
stories.body: A second crude oil tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile east of Oman, hours after another vessel exiting the Strait of Hormuz was hit, causing a small fire and blackout that was later extinguished, per The Peninsula Qatar (Oct 3). Both ships continued underway with no casualties or environmental damage reported; no group has claimed responsibility, and authorities are investigating as Tehran continues “blocking the passage of commercial ships, firing on vessels it accuses of unauthorised crossings.”

stories.headline: Houthis claim missile and drone strike on Aramco facility in Riyadh
stories.body: Yemen’s Houthi rebels claimed a ballistic missile and drone strike on an Aramco facility in Riyadh, with smoke and flames visible at the site on October 3; Saudi authorities and Aramco have not confirmed an attack, per Al Jazeera (Oct 4). Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree called the strikes “precise and direct,” saying they “led to fires breaking out” at the facility, as the Saudi-led coalition said it carried out 97 targeting operations against the Houthis, claiming over 260 fighter casualties amid intensifying fighting since a 2022 truce collapsed in July.

stories.headline: Houthis deny targeting Prophet’s Mosque power supply after Qatar’s condemnation
stories.body: The Houthis denied Saudi accusations that they struck the Taibah power station supplying Madinah’s Prophet’s Mosque, a day after Qatar condemned the attack as a violation of Islamic holy sites, per Euronews (Oct 2). Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said “our operations target its oil facilities and military bases, which are far removed from the sacred sites,” while coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki called the strike “this cowardly terrorist act” against a civilian facility; Turkey, the Arab League and Al-Azhar joined Qatar in condemning the attack.

doha_events.headline: ExxonMobil STEAM Festival continues at National Museum of Qatar
doha_events.body: The hands-on science and technology festival for families keeps running through November 28 in Temporary Exhibitions Gallery 2 at the National Museum of Qatar, with a STEAM Lab, navigation workshops and teen AR sessions continuing on weekends alongside weekday school visits. Entry is QAR 10, and with nearly two months still to go it remains one of the longest-running family draws on the October calendar, per Qatar Living (Oct 1) and Marhaba Qatar (Aug 30).

doha_events.headline: Zinatha Women’s Shopping Festival enters its final days
doha_events.body: The 9th edition of this women-only shopping showcase is in its closing stretch at Al Hazm Galleria, running 10:00 AM–11:00 PM daily through October 7 — just three days left — with fashion, beauty, accessories and lifestyle brands and free registration, per Qatar Living (Oct 1).

doha_events.headline: Ramy Sabry brings his ‘romantic sound’ to QNCC on Thursday
doha_events.body: Egyptian pop star Ramy Sabry performs a one-night concert at Qatar National Convention Centre’s Conference Hall on October 8, running 7:00 PM to 11:30 PM, promising “his signature romantic sound, fan-favourite hits and recent releases,” per Qatar Living (accessed Oct 4). Tickets are priced at QAR 795.

doha_events.headline: CardzCon brings Qatar’s first trading-card convention to Sheraton Grand Doha
doha_events.body: Qatar hosts the inaugural edition of CardzCon on October 9-10 at the Sheraton Grand Doha, with more than 70 international vendors and live activations for collectors, per The Peninsula Qatar (Sept 28). Gates open at 3:00 PM on the 9th and noon on the 10th, running to 10:00 PM both days; a one-day pass is QAR 25 for adults (QAR 15 for children 5-15, free under 5) and a two-day pass is QAR 45, via Platinumlist.

doha_events.headline: Doha Players stage ‘Silent Sky’ at THIS Theatre, Mesaimeer
doha_events.body: Doha Players open a run of Lauren Gunderson’s “Silent Sky” from October 14 to 23 at THIS Theatre in Mesaimeer, part of this October’s arts and culture line-up, per Qatar’s October events calendar reported by Qatar Living and The Peninsula Qatar (Oct 1). Tickets are available through Q-Tickets.
